name: American Nightmare
label: Equal Vision Records
lede: A Ten Yard Fight roadie turned Boston's youth-crew positivity inside out, lost his band's name to a cease and desist, saw his words turn up on Fall Out Boy records, and ended up suing WWE over the name he got back.

eras.title: The roadie's band
eras.text: Boston hardcore in the late '90s was a youth-crew revival: In My Eyes, Floorpunch, Bane, all fists and positivity. Wesley Eisold, a Virginia Beach kid working as a roadie for Ten Yard Fight, started a band that sounded like it had been listening to The Smiths and Joy Division instead.

years.src: Wikipedia: American Nightmare · Wikipedia: Wesley Eisold
years.h: Wesley Eisold, a Ten Yard Fight roadie, starts American Nightmare
years.p: In Boston, Wesley Eisold and Tim Cossar team up with Azy Relph and Jesse van Diest. The goal, per Wikipedia: something dark and nihilistic, against the scene's lyrical positivity.
years.xp:
Eisold was born in Virginia Beach in 1979, the son of a Navy officer, and was working as a roadie for Ten Yard Fight when the band started.

Eisold was born with one hand, and has said it steered him toward electronic instruments rather than guitar or drums, which shaped what he did after American Nightmare.

years.h: American Nightmare record their demo
years.p: The 1999 demo tape gets the band noticed around Boston and leads to a deal with the new local label Bridge 9 Records.

years.h: The American Nightmare EP on Bridge 9
years.p: American Nightmare's self-titled EP on Bridge 9, one of the label's first releases.

eras.title: Background Music
eras.text: Twenty-three minutes on Equal Vision Records made American Nightmare one of the most talked-about hardcore bands in the country. They took it on the road with Converge.

years.h: Background Music, 23 minutes on Equal Vision
years.p: American Nightmare's debut album, Equal Vision catalog EVR062, runs 23 minutes and 33 seconds. Wikipedia credits it with high tempos, breakdowns, gang vocals and singalongs.

years.h: The Sun Isn't Getting Any Brighter and Year One
years.p: Bridge 9 releases the The Sun Isn't Getting Any Brighter EP, and Year One gathers the early EPs with Reflections Records.

years.h: American Nightmare tour North America with Converge
years.p: In fall 2001 American Nightmare hit the road with Converge in support of Background Music.

years.h: American Nightmare cover [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]'s Depression
years.p: The band records Depression for Initial Records' Black Flag tribute Black on Black.

eras.title: A band with no name
eras.text: A Philadelphia band called American Nightmare wanted its name back, and Eisold's band spent its last year trying out new ones. They settled on Give Up the Ghost, made a second album under it, and then quit without warning.

years.big: A.N. · American Nothing · Give Up the Ghost
years.src: Wikipedia: American Nightmare · Wikipedia: Background Music · Kerrang
years.h: A cease and desist costs American Nightmare its name
years.p: A Philadelphia band also called American Nightmare threatens legal action. The Boston band goes by A.N., then American Nothing, then settles on Give Up the Ghost.
years.xp:
Kerrang reported the change in March 2003. Give Up the Ghost had been the planned title for the second album; it became the band's name instead.

Background Music was reissued in 2003 under the Give Up the Ghost name after the cease and desist, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Love American and Live in London on Bridge 9
years.p: Two more Bridge 9 releases in the band's last full year: the Love American EP and the live record Live in London.

years.h: We're Down Til We're Underground, as Give Up the Ghost
years.p: The second album, Equal Vision EVR083: 13 songs in 31 minutes. It was going to be called Give Up the Ghost until that became the band's name.

years.h: Give Up the Ghost cancel Europe, then break up the next day
years.p: In June 2004 the band cancels a European tour and a day later announces it has broken up, citing health and personal reasons.

eras.title: Poetry, synths and Fall Out Boy
eras.text: Eisold turned to poetry and electronics, and found his old lyrics coming back to him from the biggest pop-punk band in America.

years.h: Wesley Eisold starts Heartworm Press
years.p: Eisold's small press publishes zines and books, including his own poems Deathbeds (2007) and later work by Genesis P-Orridge and Boyd Rice. He also fronts the band [[Some Girls|ffee2206-eb9e-4b39-9447-8977e269ed0e]].

years.h: Wesley Eisold launches Cold Cave
years.p: Eisold's synth project [[Cold Cave|f7f32d93-0801-45cb-9f5a-e68f640649f4]] begins in 2007. It later releases records on Heartworm, Matador Records and Deathwish, including Cherish the Light Years (2011).

years.src: Wikipedia: Wesley Eisold · Wikipedia: American Nightmare
years.h: Fall Out Boy settle with Wesley Eisold over lyrics
years.p: Accused of using Eisold's lyrics, [[Fall Out Boy|516cef4d-0718-4007-9939-f9b38af3f784]] settle out of court. He is credited on The Carpal Tunnel of Love, Golden and Bang the Doldrums from Infinity on High.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the settlement also added a credit for Eisold on the multi-platinum From Under the Cork Tree (2005), where he is listed as "Inspirador."

Philly.com's Dan Goss covered the dispute in 2007.

eras.title: The name comes back
eras.text: Seven years after the split, the band reclaimed American Nightmare and played two shows on opposite coasts. Eisold eventually trademarked the name, and a new album followed.

years.h: American Nightmare reunite in Revere, Massachusetts
years.p: Announced in October via Pitchfork, the reunion is two shows: December 29, 2011 in Revere and New Year's Eve in Los Angeles. Deathwish Inc. reissues both albums.

years.h: Wesley Eisold trademarks American Nightmare
years.p: Eisold registers the American Nightmare trademark for clothing, music and entertainment, the name the band was once forced to give up.

years.h: American Nightmare on Togetherfest with Youth of Today
years.p: The band tours on Togetherfest with [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Trash Talk|3039780c-6db4-499a-8b22-ddd0bb7da0af]], Vanishing Life and Wolf Down.

years.h: American Nightmare, the first album in 15 years, on Rise
years.p: Announced on Pitchfork in December 2017, the self-titled album comes out on Rise Records, 15 years after We're Down Til We're Underground.

eras.title: The wrestler and the anniversary
eras.text: The band kept a light schedule of shows and EPs on Deathwish. Meanwhile a wrestler's nickname turned into a federal lawsuit.

years.h: Cody Rhodes gets permission to use "American Nightmare"
years.p: Eisold agrees in 2019 that wrestler Cody Runnels, known as Cody Rhodes, can use the nickname if his merchandise prominently shows his name. A 2021 agreement has similar terms.

years.h: Life Support EP on Deathwish
years.p: American Nightmare release the Life Support EP on Deathwish Inc.

years.h: Background Music 20th anniversary tour
years.p: American Nightmare tour playing Background Music in full, twenty years after its release.

years.h: Dedicated to the Next World EP
years.p: Another Deathwish EP, released in May 2023.

years.h: Wesley Eisold sues WWE and Cody Rhodes over the name
years.p: Eisold sues WWE, Cody Runnels and Fanatics, saying merch sold as American Nightmare broke the agreement by barely mentioning Runnels. He seeks at least $150,000.
years.xp: Per Fightful, the suit says fans turned up at the band's shows in Cody Rhodes merch and that social media tags got confused. Eisold asks for treble damages up to $300,000 for federal trademark infringement, plus attorney fees.

years.h: American Nightmare's 25th anniversary show in Brooklyn
years.p: The band's only show of the year is a 25th anniversary night in Brooklyn, New York.

years.h: American Nightmare play Tied Down Fest in Detroit
years.p: American Nightmare are on the 2025 bill at Tied Down Fest in Detroit.
